places.title: AUTHENTIC EXPERIENCES ACROSS EGYPT
places.sub-details: A tribute to its elusive splendor, the Egyptian landscape is quite remarkable, especially considering it’s a country composed mostly of sand and dust.
places.details: Discover the ancient civilizations of Egypt, a world of wonder where time is measured by dynasties and distance by the setting sun. The always bustling city of Cairo is a juncture of four worlds: modern and ancient, Christian and Muslim. Explore the ancient world, the three Pyramids of Giza, the majestic Sphinx, the Citadel of Salah El Din, the mosques, museums and bazaars. Sail the Nile, the world’s longest river, and discover the Valley of the Kings and Queens with the Magnificent temples and tombs along the way. The grandeur and beauty of ancient Egypt’s colossal monuments never fails to astonish. Additional impressive destinations include Saint Catherine’s Monastery, located at the foot of mystical and spiritual Mount Sinai, the sandy beaches and underwater paradise of Sharm El Sheikh and the capital of the Greco-Roman Empire, Alexandria. Once the "Pearl of the Mediterranean," Alexandria is a fascinating mix of history and modernity.

places.title: Madagascar, Land Of Discoveries And Adventures
places.sub-details: In Madagascar, you’ll be able to discover all the treasures that the island has to offer among the caring and welcoming Malagasy people.
places.details: Sometimes called "the eighth continent" for its biodiversity, Madagascar is home to 5 percent of the world’s wildlife and vegetation, most of which are exclusive to the island. Madagascar’s unique flora and fauna are matched by epic landscapes of unbelievable diversity; just 200 miles can take you from desert to rainforest and everything in between. Antananarivo is the colorful capital, with steep cobblestone streets and beautiful colonial buildings. A journey through the interior of Madagascar takes you past terraced hillsides with fertile rice fields. Along the way, you’ll interact with the welcoming Malagasy going about daily life, working in the rice paddies, tending to their zebu cattle, riding ox wagons and walking along the dusty roads with their baskets balanced precariously on their heads.Composed of two parts, the Andasibe Mantadia National Park is one of the most popular parks. The Analamazaotra is home to approximately 11 species of lemurs. However, the real attraction is the Indri, the largest lemur, whose haunting wail can be heard emanating throughout the forest. Mantadia is a bird watcher and botanist paradise with numerous waterfalls and wonderful landscapes.Madagascar’s sights are endless. Explore the red iron oxide pinnacles of the Tsingy Rouge National Park and the Jurrassic beauty of the desert canyon of Isalo National Park, where erosion has carved the sandstone into fantastic shapes. Discover dazzling beaches with some of the world’s best snorkelling and diving sites and watch the sun set in the Avenue of the Baobabs.Travel through Madagascar often comes with delayed flights, dirt roads and basic accommodation, but all of this adds to its allure and charm. It is a wonderful destination for outdoor lovers and those who relish adventure.

places.title: Explore Uganda, The Pearl Of Africa
places.sub-details: Uganda is truly undiscovered. From unique encounters with mountain gorillas or chimps to wildlife safaris and boat cruises, you’ll be inspired for a lifetime.
places.details: Often described as the "Pearl of Africa," this lush land is celebrated for its primate population and fine scenery. Uganda has been attracting active adventure travelers to the Bwindi Impenetrable Forest to view the endangered mountain gorillas for many years. Tread softly and observe these fascinating mammals as they go about their daily grooming and foraging rituals.Uganda’s other pearls include Queen Elizabeth National Park, which offers a complimentary traditional East Africa big game safari experience. This park is home to lion, elephant, hyena and the giant forest hog, to name just a few. An afternoon boat cruise on the Kazinga Channel is the perfect way to end the day as the animals and birds come to the water. Kibale Forest National Park is another destination where you put on your hiking boots and set out in hopes of finding chimpanzees. Murchison National Park’s main attraction is Murchison Falls, as well as the River Nile, with its resident hippo and crocodile population.

places.title: The Beautiful Islands Of Africa
places.sub-details: Africa’s beautiful islands are the perfect places to escape to whether it’s for a honeymoon, wrapping up a safari family getaway or adventure trip.
places.details: Seychelles   For anyone looking for unspoiled tropical paradise hundreds of miles from anywhere, where one can lie on palm-fringed beaches, swim in warm, crystal-clear topaz seas and just relax, the Seychelles islands are the answer. A haven for honeymooners, fisherman and families alike this island destination complements the African safari experience perfectly.     Mozambique   Mozambique, whose coastline extends from South Africa to Tanzania, is known for its pristine, less-traveled beach destinations along the Indian Ocean. Long, dune-fringed beaches, turquoise waters, well-preserved corals and remote archipelagos make this the ideal destination for honeymooners, families and those looking for adventure.    Zanzibar   The perfect place to relax and wrap up your safari is the spice island of Zanzibar. It is a slumbering paradise where green cloves, bread leaf, rice, cinnamon and coconuts grow. The annals of Zanzibar read like a chapter from "The Thousand and One Nights" and doubtlessly evoke many exotic images in the minds of travelers to its shores for centuries, some in search of trade, some in search of plunder and still others in search of an idyllic home.   Mauritius With its sapphire waters, powder-white beaches and luxury resorts, Mauritius is the perfect beach complement to a Southern Africa safari. The island’s allure appeals to honeymooners and families alike. The island is famous for watersports, the white beaches of Palmar and Belle Mare, and Tamarin Bay.

places.title: Rwanda, The Land Of A Thousand Hills
places.sub-details: Rwanda’s stunning scenery offers some of the most unique experiences. It is here that you can catch a glimpse of the magnificent mountain gorillas.
places.details: Visiting Rwanda, "the land of a thousand hills," is one of the great wildlife adventures on the planet. The welcoming people, rich landscapes and wildlife attractions make Rwanda an ideal addition to any African safari. Rwanda is mountainous, green and lush, and home to a variety of primates, more than 100 orchids and over 600 bird species - a paradise for bird watchers, conservationists and botanists alike.The star attraction is the highly endangered mountain gorilla. An encounter with a silverback gorilla and his family can be a hair-raising experience and one you will likely never forget! Their human-like characteristics are fascinating, and to observe them grooming, foraging and nesting is a privilege. The young juveniles are playful and mischievous.While the majority of tourism is focused on a visit to the Parc National des Volcans in the north, the nearby Lake Kivu offers a great place to unwind after a trekking adventure. For those with a bit more time, Nyunge National Park offers a pristine mountain rainforest, which is home to habituated chimpanzees and other primate species.It’s definitely time to put on your boots and visit Rwanda.

places.title: Experience The Sheer Natural Beauty Of Namibia
places.sub-details: Namibia is a country that charms its way into your soul. You can be assured that even though you leave Namibia after your trip, Namibia will never leave you.
places.details: Namibia is a place of great contrasts, characterized by vast open spaces, endless horizons and dramatic landscapes. The country’s rare plant species, magnificent wildlife and incredible night skies offer some of the most mesmerizing scenery in the world.The Fish River Canyon in the south cuts an impressive 100-mile long gorge into an otherwise flat landscape, while the iconic red sand dunes of Sossusvlei tower more than 900 feet above the surrounding plains. With its shimmering salt pans, Etosha National Park is Namibia’s premier wildlife destination. Large herds of plains game concentrate around the waterholes in the dry season, while the summer rainfall welcomes abundant new life.In the north, the haunting and evocative Skeleton Coast is known for its swirling mists and shipwreck strewn shorelines. The Kunene region, with its stark plains and ancient valleys, is one of the harshest environments on the planet. Here, the most reliable water source is the fog created by the cold Atlantic Ocean and warm air of the desert. Yet, this living desert thrives with life in all its unique and varied forms, from the bizarre Welwitschia plant and solitary oryx to the rare brown hyena and desert-adapted rhinos and elephants.For a truly off-the-beaten-path experience, venture to the remote north home to the statuesque Himba, one of the last true nomadic tribes on earth. Namibia’s hidden treasures are for those who appreciate an unspoiled and authentic experience.

places.title: Discover The Best Of Zambia
places.sub-details: The land of the legendary African walking safari, Victoria Falls, the wild Zambezi River, abundant wildlife, and raw wilderness, all in one friendly country.
places.details: Regarded as one of the last true wildernesses, Zambia is probably southern Africa’s best-kept secret. Home to the mighty Victoria Falls, it is the country’s interior parks that will delight those seeking a more off-the-beaten-path safari. The intimate camps offer a highly personalized safari bush experience that keeps guests coming back time and time again. The South Luangwa National Park is the place to experience the original walking safari, a "heart-thumping" way to get close to nature and feel her pulse. The Luangwa River and oxbow lagoons are home to hippos and crocodiles and frequently visited by elephants, Thornicroft giraffes and buffalo. This park is one of the best in Africa to view leopards in their natural environment.Kafue National Park offers a remote and exclusive safari experience. Game drives on the Busanga Plains in search of lions, puku and red lechwe can only be outdone by the option to take a hot air balloon safari and float quietly above the same great wilderness.Another favorite is the Lower Zambezi National Park. Day and night game drives, walking safaris, canoe trips, river safaris, catch and release angling for tiger fish and time spent in photographic hides leave you wishing you had planned a longer stay.

places.title: Machu Picchu, Peru
places.sub-details: Peru is a country rich in ancient culture, diverse landscapes, and vibrant cities. It offers coastal deserts, Andean mountains, and Amazonian jungles.

top-location.title: Machu Picchu
top-location.details: A UNESCO World Heritage site and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World, this ancient Inca citadel is set high in the Andes.

top-location.title: Cusco
top-location.details: The historical capital of the Inca Empire, known for its colonial architecture and archaeological remains.

top-location.title: Sacred Valley
top-location.details: A lush region with charming villages, agricultural terraces, and ancient ruins.

top-location.title: Nazca Lines
top-location.details: Mysterious geoglyphs in the desert.

places.title: Patagonia (Argentina & Chile)
places.sub-details: Known for tango, steak, and vibrant culture, Argentina boasts diverse landscapes from the Pampas to the Andes. A land of contrasts, Chile stretches from the Atacama Desert in the north to the icy fjords in the south.

top-location.title: Torres del Paine National Park (Chile)
top-location.details: Renowned for its granite peaks, glacial lakes, and diverse wildlife.

top-location.title: Perito Moreno Glacier (Argentina)
top-location.details: A massive advancing glacier in Los Glaciares National Park.

top-location.title: Ushuaia (Argentina)
top-location.details: The southernmost city in the world, a gateway to Antarctica.

places.title: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
places.sub-details: Brazil is the largest country in South America, known for its tropical rainforests, lively cities, and rich cultural heritage.

top-location.title: Christ the Redeemer
top-location.details: One of the world's most iconic statues atop Corcovado Mountain.

top-location.title: Copacabana Beach
top-location.details: A world-famous beach known for its vibrant atmosphere.

top-location.title: Sugarloaf Mountain
top-location.details: Offers panoramic views of Rio and its coastline.

top-location.title: Tijuca National Park
top-location.details: A rainforest within the city, great for hiking and wildlife.

places.title: Galápagos Islands, Ecuador
places.sub-details: Ecuador offers a blend of Andean highlands, Amazonian rainforests, and Pacific coastline.

top-location.title: Galápagos Islands
top-location.details: Famous for its unique wildlife, including giant tortoises, marine iguanas, and blue-footed boobies.

top-location.title: Quito
top-location.details: The capital, known for its well-preserved colonial center and proximity to the equator.

top-location.title: Otavalo Market
top-location.details: A vibrant indigenous market offering traditional crafts.

places.title: Salar de Uyuni, Bolivia
places.sub-details: Bolivia is a landlocked country with high-altitude landscapes, salt flats, and indigenous cultures.

top-location.title: Salar de Uyuni
top-location.details: The world’s largest salt flat, a surreal landscape that reflects the sky during the wet season.

top-location.title: La Paz
top-location.details: The world's highest capital city, offering stunning views and cultural experiences.

top-location.title: Lake Titicaca
top-location.details: The highest navigable lake in the world, shared with Peru.

places.title: Antarctic Peninsula
places.sub-details: Antarctica is the coldest, driest, and windiest continent, home to pristine landscapes and unique wildlife.

top-location.title: Lemaire Channel
top-location.details: A narrow passage with towering icebergs and dramatic cliffs.

top-location.title: Paradise Bay
top-location.details: Known for its spectacular glacial scenery and abundant wildlife, including penguins and seals.

top-location.title: Deception Island
top-location.details: A volcanic island with a natural harbor and unique geothermal activity.

places.title: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
places.sub-details: A British Overseas Territory, this remote area is often visited as part of Antarctic expeditions.

top-location.title: King Edward Point
top-location.details: The administrative center with a rich history of exploration.

top-location.title: St. Andrews Bay
top-location.details: Known for its massive king penguin colonies.

top-location.title: Grytviken
top-location.details: A historic whaling station and the final resting place of explorer Sir Ernest Shackleton.

title: UK & EUROPE
details: Europe is a continent filled with a rich tapestry of history, culture, and breathtaking landscapes. Here’s a detailed guide to some of the best countries in Europe and their most popular and beautiful locations to visit:

places.title: France
places.sub-details: Renowned for its art, fashion, and gastronomy, France is the epitome of romance and sophistication.

top-location.title: Paris
top-location.details: Visit the Eiffel Tower, Louvre Museum, Notre-Dame Cathedral, and stroll along the Seine River.

top-location.title: Provence
top-location.details: Lavender fields, vineyards, and charming villages.

top-location.title: French Riviera (Côte d'Azur)
top-location.details: Glamorous beaches in Nice, Cannes, and Monaco.

top-location.title: Loire Valley
top-location.details: Known for its chateaux and vineyards.

top-location.title: Mont Saint-Michel
top-location.details: A stunning island commune with an abbey.

places.title: Italy
places.sub-details: A land of ancient ruins, exquisite cuisine, and breathtaking art.

top-location.title: Rome
top-location.details: Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Vatican City (St. Peter’s Basilica & Sistine Chapel).

top-location.title: Florence
top-location.details: Uffizi Gallery, Florence Cathedral, and the Ponte Vecchio.

top-location.title: Venice
top-location.details: Gondola rides on the canals and St. Mark's Basilica.

top-location.title: Amalfi Coast
top-location.details: Picturesque coastal villages like Positano and Ravello.

top-location.title: Tuscany
top-location.details: Rolling hills, vineyards, and medieval towns.

places.title: Spain
places.sub-details: A mix of vibrant traditions, flamenco dancing, and sunny beaches.

top-location.title: Barcelona
top-location.details: Sagrada Família, Park Güell, and La Rambla.

top-location.title: Madrid
top-location.details: Prado Museum and Royal Palace.

top-location.title: Granada
top-location.details: Alhambra Palace and Generalife Gardens.

top-location.title: Seville
top-location.details: Alcázar of Seville and Flamenco performances.

top-location.title: Balearic Islands (Mallorca, Ibiza)
top-location.details: Stunning beaches and nightlife.

places.title: Greece
places.sub-details: Famous for its ancient ruins, crystal-clear waters, and iconic white-washed buildings.

top-location.title: Athens
top-location.details: Acropolis, Parthenon, and Ancient Agora.

top-location.title: Santorini
top-location.details: White and blue architecture with caldera views.

top-location.title: Mykonos
top-location.details: Known for its vibrant nightlife and beaches.

top-location.title: Crete
top-location.details: Knossos Palace and stunning beaches like Elafonisi.

top-location.title: Meteora
top-location.details: Monasteries perched on towering rock formations.

places.title: Switzerland
places.sub-details: A paradise for nature lovers with its snow-capped mountains and pristine lakes.

top-location.title: Zermatt
top-location.details: Iconic Matterhorn mountain and skiing.

top-location.title: Lucerne
top-location.details: Chapel Bridge and Lake Lucerne.

top-location.title: Interlaken
top-location.details: Adventure sports and access to Jungfraujoch.

top-location.title: Geneva
top-location.details: Jet d'Eau fountain and United Nations headquarters.

top-location.title: Zurich
top-location.details: Old Town (Altstadt) and Lake Zurich.

places.title: Germany
places.sub-details: A blend of medieval towns, modern cities, and rich history.

top-location.title: Berlin
top-location.details: Brandenburg Gate, Berlin Wall, and Museum Island.

top-location.title: Munich
top-location.details: Oktoberfest and Neuschwanstein Castle.

top-location.title: Heidelberg
top-location.details: Romantic old town and Heidelberg Castle.

top-location.title: Black Forest
top-location.details: Fairy-tale landscapes and cuckoo clocks.

top-location.title: Hamburg
top-location.details: Port city with canals and Speicherstadt.

places.title: United Kingdom
places.sub-details: A mix of bustling cities and serene countryside.

top-location.title: London
top-location.details: Buckingham Palace, Big Ben, and British Museum.

top-location.title: Edinburgh
top-location.details: Edinburgh Castle and Royal Mile.

top-location.title: Lake District
top-location.details: Stunning lakes and walking trails.

top-location.title: Bath
top-location.details: Roman baths and Georgian architecture.

top-location.title: Stonehenge
top-location.details: Prehistoric monument.

places.title: Austria
places.sub-details: Famous for its classical music heritage and Alpine scenery.

top-location.title: Vienna
top-location.details: Schönbrunn Palace and Vienna Opera House.

top-location.title: Salzburg
top-location.details: Birthplace of Mozart and Hohensalzburg Fortress.

top-location.title: Hallstatt
top-location.details: Picturesque lakeside village.

top-location.title: Innsbruck
top-location.details: Alpine activities and Golden Roof.

top-location.title: Graz
top-location.details: UNESCO-listed old town.

places.title: Netherlands
places.sub-details: Known for its windmills, tulip fields, and canals.

top-location.title: Amsterdam
top-location.details: Anne Frank House, Van Gogh Museum, and canal cruises.

top-location.title: Rotterdam
top-location.details: Modern architecture and vibrant culture.

top-location.title: Keukenhof
top-location.details: Expansive tulip gardens.

top-location.title: Zaanse Schans
top-location.details: Traditional windmills and Dutch culture.

top-location.title: Utrecht
top-location.details: Historic city with canals and churches.

places.title: Norway
places.sub-details: Land of fjords, northern lights, and rugged natural beauty.

top-location.title: Oslo
top-location.details: Vigeland Park and Viking Ship Museum.

top-location.title: Bergen
top-location.details: Gateway to fjords and colorful Bryggen.

top-location.title: Geirangerfjord
top-location.details: Iconic fjord with waterfalls.

top-location.title: Tromsø
top-location.details: Northern lights and Arctic adventures.

top-location.title: Lofoten Islands
top-location.details: Dramatic peaks and fishing villages.

places.title: Portugal
places.sub-details: A coastal haven with historic towns and warm hospitality.

top-location.title: Lisbon
top-location.details: Belém Tower and Alfama district.

top-location.title: Porto
top-location.details: Douro River and wine cellars.

top-location.title: Algarve
top-location.details: Golden beaches and sea caves.

top-location.title: Sintra
top-location.details: Pena Palace and Quinta da Regaleira.

top-location.title: Madeira
top-location.details: Scenic hikes and lush landscapes.

places.title: Iceland
places.sub-details: A land of volcanic landscapes, geysers, and glaciers.

top-location.title: Reykjavik
top-location.details: Blue Lagoon and Hallgrimskirkja Church.

top-location.title: Golden Circle
top-location.details: Geysir, Gullfoss waterfall, and Thingvellir National Park.

top-location.title: Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon
top-location.details: Icebergs and seals.

top-location.title: Vik
top-location.details: Black sand beaches and basalt columns.

top-location.title: Northern Lights
top-location.details: Best seen in winter months.

sub-details.heading: Geography
sub-details.details: Situated on the Persian Gulf's southeastern coast, Dubai is the largest city in the UAE.

sub-details.heading: Climate
sub-details.details: Dubai experiences a hot desert climate with sunny weather throughout the year.

sub-details.heading: Culture
sub-details.details: A mix of Emirati heritage and a cosmopolitan vibe due to its expatriate population.

sub-details.heading: Economy
sub-details.details: Known for its trade, tourism, and luxury real estate industries.

top-location.title: Burj Khalifa
top-location.details: The tallest building in the world at 828 meters (2,717 ft), the Burj Khalifa is an architectural masterpiece.
highlights: Observation decks on the 124th, 125th, and 148th floors.
A view of Dubai’s skyline and surrounding desert.
Light and fountain shows at the base in Burj Lake.

top-location.title: The Dubai Mall
top-location.details: One of the world's largest shopping malls, it is a hub for luxury shopping, dining, and entertainment.
highlights: Dubai Aquarium & Underwater Zoo.
VR Park for virtual reality experiences.
Ice Rink and KidZania for families.
The Fountain Show just outside the mall.

note.title: Tip
note.details: Allocate a full day to explore.

top-location.title: Palm Jumeirah
top-location.details: A man-made island shaped like a palm tree, known for its luxury resorts.
highlights: Atlantis, The Palm (resort with an aquarium and water park).
Beach clubs like Club Vista Mare.
Dine at Nobu or other high-end restaurants.
Speedboat tours for a panoramic view.

note.title: Best Activity
note.details: Enjoying the beach or water sports.

top-location.title: Dubai Marina
top-location.details: A canal city with modern skyscrapers, luxury yachts, and waterside dining.
highlights: The Marina Walk with restaurants and shops.
Yacht cruises for a luxurious experience.
Jumeirah Beach Residence (JBR) for beach and nightlife.

note.title: Best Activity
note.details: Dhow cruise dinner for an illuminated view of the skyline.

top-location.title: Desert Safari
top-location.details: Explore Dubai’s vast desert landscapes on a thrilling adventure.
highlights: Dune bashing in 4x4 vehicles.
Camel riding and sandboarding.
Traditional Emirati dinner and cultural shows.

note.title: Best Time
note.details: Late afternoon to enjoy the sunset and evening entertainment.

top-location.title: Dubai Creek
top-location.details: The historical heart of Dubai, dividing the city into Deira and Bur Dubai.
highlights: Traditional abra (boat) rides.
Explore souks like the Gold Souk and Spice Souk.
Visit Al Fahidi Historical District and Dubai Museum.

top-location.title: Dubai Frame
top-location.details: A giant picture frame offering stunning views of old and new Dubai.
highlights: Glass-bottom bridge for an exhilarating experience.
History gallery showcasing Dubai’s transformation.

top-location.title: Jumeirah Mosque
top-location.details: A fine example of Islamic architecture open to non-Muslims for guided tours.
highlights: Learn about Islamic culture and traditions.
Beautiful lighting at night.

top-location.title: Global Village
top-location.details: A multicultural festival park offering entertainment, shopping, and dining.
highlights: Pavilions from countries around the world.
Live performances and fireworks.
Cultural and handicraft exhibitions.

top-location.title: Ain Dubai (Dubai Eye)
top-location.details: The world’s largest observation wheel on Bluewaters Island.
highlights: Stunning views of the city and coastline.
Dining options at the base of the wheel.

note.title: Tip
note.details: Ride during sunset or at night for city lights.

top-location.title: Dubai Opera
top-location.details: A state-of-the-art cultural and performing arts center.
highlights: Enjoy operas, ballets, concerts, and theatre productions.
Unique dhow-shaped architecture.

top-location.title: Ski Dubai
top-location.details: An indoor ski resort located in Mall of the Emirates.
highlights: Skiing and snowboarding on five slopes.
Interactions with penguins.

top-location.title: La Mer
top-location.details: A beachfront destination with trendy cafes, boutiques, and a water park.
highlights: Laguna Waterpark for families.
Instagram-worthy street art and murals.

top-location.title: The Walk at JBR
top-location.details: A bustling promenade near the beach with shops, cafes, and entertainment.
highlights: Open-air market and cinema.
Live street performances.

note.title: Evening Plan
note.details: Dinner with a view of the beach.
